analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata against the indexed threat model and selected T-041 detail. StartCommand.swift:174-179 adds model-dependent wired-memory advice before the serving-mode split; StatusCommand.swift:64,102,172-175 passes hardware into advice for a recorded load error. These visible changes print diagnostics, not execute privileged commands, alter serving authorization or change encryption. Existing trust/readiness displays remain unchanged. No concrete regression is established in these callers.
GLMWiredLimitAdviceTests.swift:44-88,102-133 specifies hardware/model gating, static sysctl advice and a persistent root LaunchDaemon guide, and distinguishes Metal OOM from load-admission failure. Integration should inspect GLMWiredLimitAdvice and GLM5NextWiredLimit implementations for bounded live reads, safe fixed privileged-command content, and the availability implications of raised system-wide wiring limits (TB-003/TB-007). Tests do not prove those implementation properties.
RegistrationWeightHashTests.swift patch head:28-50 specifies reuse of a persisted GLM registration hash without rereading weights and invalidation after an ordinary weight write; head:53-73 requires full hashing for other models and recordless starts. This requires integration review of registrationWeightHash and its record validation against an adversarial operator (A-004, T-012/T-027), including record tampering, filesystem identity changes and the relationship to load-time verification and T-041's verified weightHash cache binding. Those implementations are absent here, so neither a forged-hash regression nor preservation of the binding can be concluded from these tests. No visible change affects tokens, attestation, billing, fan authority or plaintext handling. Remaining uncertainty is material to the new hash-reuse contract, not evidence of a vulnerability.
